overall_why: A and B are both new ideas and both clearly beat the old design. C has a new frame, but the old lesson is still inside it. A over B was close. B is calmer and quicker to start: three lines and a caret (concept-b/shots/s1-cold-dark, concept-b/view/window/s1-cold-dark). A wins mine, flexible, clarity and craft. What tipped it was scenario 3. In A, when the plan changes, the plan document opens beside the lesson with each moved item's old date struck through and a change bar beside it. That happens with the stand-in (concept-a/view/window/s3-after-dark, concept-a/shots/s3-after-light) and with the real Claude Code (concept-a/view/live/s3-after-dark, all four re-dated blocks marked). B's real lesson leaves only a one-line note at the foot, and the tutor's reply isn't on screen in that capture (concept-b/view/live/s3-after-dark). A also explains a missing mark ('No mark, not taken as the answer', my turn), where B shows nothing. It treats settings and the plan as plain files the learner owns (concept-a/shots/settings-dark, plan-edit-dark). B over C: B rebuilt the lesson as well as the shell. C kept the old lesson's parts: margin mark labels, a green bar on the task, and the Hint / I'm lost / I don't know row (concept-c/shots/s2-answer-dark). Its course sheet still prints 'level 3 of 10', 'due today' and raw '$V_{max}$' (concept-c/shots/course-dark). In C's demo, 'back to the task' returns to a question already answered right (concept-c/shots/s4-return-dark).

by_measure_why.mine: A works like the editors the client named. You see your own files under their own names in tabs and a sidebar (concept-a/shots/sidebar-dark). ⌘P opens any document (concept-a/shots/open-dark). Settings are a text file that takes any font, colour or key (concept-a/shots/settings-dark). The plan is your own plan.md, which you can edit (concept-a/shots/plan-edit-dark). The lesson reopens with your half-written working (concept-a/shots/s5-week-dark). B is a close second. It has almost no app voice, a settings layer with 'Edit as text' (concept-b/shots/settings-dark), and every layer is keyboard-driven. But the plan, your work and your material only ever appear as overlays the app summons; you never see them as your own documents. C still has an app voice ('Your earlier days will be here.', concept-c/view/window/s2-answer-dark). It asks you to write where you stopped (concept-c/shots/stop-dark), and its settings sheet has fewer options (concept-c/shots/settings-dark).
by_measure_why.calm: B's cold screen is three lines and a caret in both schemes and after a week away (concept-b/shots/s1-cold-light, s5-week-dark), and the lesson is one column. A at rest shows a tab, the title, the task, 'Stopped on …' and a Continue pill (concept-a/shots/s1-cold-dark); in the lesson it adds only a status line. C's cold page is calm (concept-c/shots/s1-cold-dark). But its lesson shows the most at once: the answer line, then Hint / I'm lost / I don't know / Photo / Symbols, then a second 'Or write on the page' line, plus timestamps and a plan agenda in the margin (concept-c/shots/s2-answer-dark). That tipped A over C.
by_measure_why.easy_to_start: In my B turn, the caret was already in the line and one Return started the lesson; '↩ start' / '↩ carry on' names exactly what Return does (concept-b/view/window/s1-cold-dark). A is one key too: 'Continue Return' with your draft kept (concept-a/shots/s1-cold-light), or 'What do you want to work on?' with the plan's next item filled in (concept-a/view/window/s1-cold-dark). Its first run, though, is a 'Magnesium' welcome page with three bordered buttons (concept-a/shots/s1-cold-first-dark). C is also one key ('Pick up where you stopped on Tuesday', concept-c/shots/s1-cold-dark), but once you're in, five help words and two lines make you choose before you write.
by_measure_why.flexible: All three tell talk from answers by where you type, not by a label, and none shows being off-plan as being behind. A shows a plan change most fully: a split pane with struck-through old dates and moved-up / moved-down marks, both with the stand-in and live (concept-a/view/window/s3-after-dark, concept-a/view/live/s3-after-dark). ⌘E lets you edit the plan yourself. B puts a 'The plan changed' card under the tutor's reply and has a ⌘P layer that marks moved rows (concept-b/view/window/s3-after-dark, my turn). In the live run, though, only a one-line note showed (concept-b/view/live/s3-after-dark). C's agenda says 'Moved from Sun 22 Nov' but drops the per-item dates (concept-c/view/live/s3-after-dark). Its ⌘P sheet marks nothing that moved, and the demo goes back to the wrong task (concept-c/shots/s4-return-dark).
by_measure_why.craft: A runs the most kinds of surface: tabs, a status bar, a split pane, a palette, and settings and the record as documents. It keeps them consistent, and the narrow size stays clean (concept-a/shots/narrow-lesson-light, s3-after-light). Its faults are the pinned task strip sitting over a ghosted 'Your answer' (concept-a/shots/s4-offplan-dark) and a heavy blue pill. B's faces and layers are refined (concept-b/shots/plan-dark), but it has visible faults. The fading header shows sliced glyph fragments (concept-b/shots/s2-answer-dark, s5-week-next-dark). The mark is printed twice (concept-b/shots/s2-answer-dark). At the narrow size the answer line has no question in view above it (concept-b/shots/narrow-lesson-dark). C has the most faults. The cold column is pushed left, leaving a dead right third (concept-c/shots/s1-cold-dark). It shows raw LaTeX (concept-c/shots/course-dark) and 'K m' (concept-c/shots/stop-dark). At the narrow size the margin labels nearly touch the edge (concept-c/shots/narrow-lesson-dark).
by_measure_why.clarity: A's status line always names the next key: 'Esc to say something else', 'Tab: back to the task', 'Plan changed at 18:15', 'The tutor is writing' (concept-a/shots/s3-before-dark, s3-after-dark). In my turn it said why a retry had no mark. B's hints are clear ('esc talk instead', '↑ answer'), but a retry with no mark shows nothing. 'From earlier' and '⌘K start without them' leave you asking who 'them' is (concept-b/shots/s5-week-light). C labels its two lines well. But the demo returns to an already-answered question while saying 'You were on step 3' (concept-c/shots/s4-return-light), and the cold page ends with placeholder copy.
by_measure_why.performance: This is effectively a tie. Input latency is identical in every perf.json (median 17, p95 19, max 20 ms), and the same again in my turns. Startup per perf.json: A 809/628/575 ms (mean 671), B 850/620/567 (mean 679), C 805/615/644 (mean 688). C's week reopen, 644 ms, is the slowest single start among the three. My turns measured A 771, B 754, C 831 ms. The order follows perf.json; A and B are within noise, and C is last on both sources.

concept-a: The task's field still says 'Your answer' (concept-a/shots/s2-answer-dark), the very box wording the brief objected to, though CONCEPT.md says the field has no label. Also, the talk line is a bare rule with no cue on the page itself (concept-a/shots/s4-offplan-dark).
The pinned task strip overlaps the ghosted 'Your answer' of the scrolled-away field at the top of the pane (concept-a/shots/s4-offplan-dark, s4-offplan-light).

The app's own voice and weight at the door: the first-run 'Magnesium' welcome page with checkmarks and three bordered buttons (concept-a/shots/s1-cold-first-dark), and a saturated blue 'Continue [Return]' pill that is the heaviest object on otherwise quiet pages (concept-a/shots/s1-cold-light).
concept-b: The record's latest fact is printed twice, under the answer and again under the line ('Marked right, on your own.' x2 in concept-b/shots/s2-answer-dark and narrow-lesson-dark; 'Not right yet.' x2 in my turn).
The fading top edge slices text into glyph fragments instead of hiding it (concept-b/shots/s2-answer-dark, s3-after-dark, s5-week-next-dark 'Biochemistry').

A retry with no mark gets no word at all (my turn). The plan is only ever an overlay or a one-line note: in the live lesson the change showed as one line at the foot, with the tutor's reply out of view (concept-b/view/live/s3-after-dark). And '⌘K start without them' has no antecedent (concept-b/shots/s5-week-dark).
concept-c: The old lesson is kept inside the new frame: green bar on the task, margin labels for marks, the Hint / I'm lost / I don't know row plus Photo and Symbols, and a second 'Or write on the page' line under every task (concept-c/shots/s2-answer-dark). It even opens with 'Welcome back… Quick check 1' (concept-c/shots/s5-week-next-dark).
Old vocabulary and broken text in the sheets: 'level 3 of 10', 'due today', raw '$V_{max}$' (concept-c/shots/course-dark), and 'K m' prefilled in the stop line (concept-c/shots/stop-dark).

'Back to the task' returns to a question already marked right, while saying 'You were on step 3' (concept-c/shots/s4-return-dark). The cold column is pushed left, leaving a dead right third (concept-c/shots/s1-cold-dark). The plan sheet marks nothing that moved (my turn).

concept-a.why: The old Library -> Course -> Lesson -> Proofs pages are gone. The window opens on the last open document. You move by tabs, two panes, ⌘P and a status line. The plan is the learner's plan.md, shown beside the lesson when it changes. Progress is a dated Record document with no levels, proof dots, due counts or study-day strip (concept-a/shots/record-dark vs baseline progress.jpg, summary.jpg). Settings are a file. What carries over is small and only in the lesson: a serif reading face, a left-ruled task block, the mark in the left gutter beside the answer (as in the old 'Your answer / Marked right' gutter), and the words 'Your answer' as the field's placeholder.

concept-b.why: There are no screens at all. The window is one surface whose rest state is three lines and a caret, Spotlight-style (concept-b/shots/s1-cold-dark vs baseline library.jpg). Everything else (courses, plan, material, past work, settings, help) is the same summoned layer over where you are. The old ⌘K menu was a side door; here it is the only door. The answer line sits inside the task and talk has its own › line, replacing the old 'Your answer' box with Hint / I don't know / I'm lost. The old step strip, levels, proofs, due counts, summary page and week strip are all gone, and progress is ⌘Y, dated marks in words (concept-b/shots/work-dark).

concept-c.why: The frame is new: a dated logbook page as the first screen, earlier days below, the plan as an agenda in the margin, and sheets in place of pages (concept-c/shots/s1-cold-dark vs baseline library.jpg). The lesson inside is the old one rearranged. Green marks sit in the left margin ('right / unaided', where the old gutter said 'Your answer / Marked right'). There's a green bar on the open task, the same Hint / I'm lost / I don't know row under the answer, and 'Welcome back… Quick check 1' (concept-c/shots/s2-answer-dark, s5-week-next-dark vs baseline session.jpg, session-marked.jpg). The course sheet is the old Course page as a drawer, still printing a level and due days (concept-c/shots/course-dark vs baseline course.jpg).

window_turns: Each build got the same keyboard-only script in the release window: photo cold; Return to start; 'b = 5'; 'b = -5'; Esc then 'I skipped three days and the midterm moved, change the plan'; 'By the way, why do we divide by n - 1 …'; 'OK, back to the task.'; perf; ⌘P; end. With this tutor the task was a standard-error question, so 'b = -5' got no mark from the record in all three; each window showed that honestly. B (light, ~1.5 min): it opened on 'Sampling distributions / ↩ start' with the caret in the line, and Return started the lesson. 'Not right yet.' appeared under the answer and again at the foot; the 'b = -5' retry showed nothing. Esc moved the line to talk (›). The plan change drew a 'The plan changed' card under the reply plus a foot line. 'Back to the task' made the task live again with the caret in it, and ⌘P showed the plan layer with moved rows and new days. Startup 754 ms, input median 17 / p95 19 ms. A (dark, ~1 min after a 4.5 min wait): it opened on 'New lesson / What do you want to work on?' with the plan's first item filled in, and Return started the lesson. The gutter showed × 'Not right yet', then – 'No mark, not taken as the answer'. Esc moved to the talk line. The plan change opened 'Midterm 2 plan' in a pane beside the lesson, with old dates struck through, 'moved up/down', and 'Plan changed at 18:56 · Tab: back to the task' in the status line. 'Back to the task' put the caret back into the task block, and ⌘P listed lessons, the plan file, material and the Record. Startup 771 ms, input 17 / 19 ms. C (light, ~1 min after a 6 min wait): it opened on 'Thursday 12 November / Start on Midterm 2 [Return]', and Return started the lesson. The margin showed 'not right', then 'no mark'. Esc moved to 'Or write on the page'. The agenda changed in place ('Moved from Sun 22 Nov', moved up/down), with a timed 'The plan changed.' line. 'Back to the task' re-posed the right task with the Hint row under it. ⌘P opened a right-hand sheet that lists the plan without marking what moved. Startup 831 ms, input 17 / 18 ms. I closed every window with final-turn.sh end.
